# Writing integers

Spelling an integer as text: sign, base prefix, zero padding and digits.

<h2 id="max-decimal-digits"><code>MaxDecimalDigits</code></h2>

```rux
pub const MaxDecimalDigits: uint = 20;
```

The most digits a `uint64` ever needs, for 18446744073709551615.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/Digits.rux#L9)

<h2 id="write-uint"><code>WriteUint</code></h2>

```rux
pub func WriteUint(cursor: &var ByteCursor, value: uint64)
```

Writes the decimal digits of an unsigned value.
A division loop produces them least significant first, so they land in a small buffer and go back reversed.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/Digits.rux#L16)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                            |
| -------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `cursor` | `&var ByteCursor` | the buffer the digits are written into |
| `value`  | `uint64`          | the value to act on                    |

<h2 id="write-int"><code>WriteInt</code></h2>

```rux
pub func WriteInt(cursor: &var ByteCursor, value: int64)
```

Writes the sign, then the magnitude.
The magnitude is taken in `uint64` rather than by negating within `int64`, because the most negative `int64` has
no positive counterpart there: negating it overflows straight back to itself. Two's complement gives the right
answer for that value and for every other one.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/Digits.rux#L45)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type              | Description                            |
| -------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `cursor` | `&var ByteCursor` | the buffer the digits are written into |
| `value`  | `int64`           | the value to act on                    |

<h2 id="write-integer-digits"><code>WriteIntegerDigits</code></h2>

```rux
pub func WriteIntegerDigits(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec,
    digits: char8[..],
    count: uint,
    negative: bool
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes an integer whose digits are already produced, applying sign, prefix, zero-padding and alignment.
`digits` holds the digits least significant first, which is the order a division loop makes them; `count` says
how many. Zero-padding puts its zeros between the sign and the digits and wins over alignment when both are
asked for. Nothing here allocates or copies the digits: each piece goes to the writer as it is reached.
Reports whatever the writer reported, stopping at the first refusal.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/IntegerText.rux#L24)

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type              | Description                                          |
| ---------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `writer`   | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                                      |
| `spec`     | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for                       |
| `digits`   | `char8[..]`       | the decimal or based digits, least significant first |
| `count`    | `uint`            | how many entries of `digits` are meaningful          |
| `negative` | `bool`            | whether a minus sign precedes the digits             |

**Returns**: success when the complete rendering was accepted

<h2 id="write-integer-spec"><code>WriteIntegerSpec</code></h2>

```rux
pub func WriteIntegerSpec(
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec,
    magnitude: uint64,
    negative: bool
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes an integer under the whole of `spec`: base, sign, alternate prefix, zero-padding and alignment.
`magnitude` is the absolute value and `negative` its sign, kept apart because the most negative value of a
signed width has no positive counterpart to negate into.
Reports whatever the writer reported.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/IntegerText.rux#L79)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type              | Description                    |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer`    | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`      | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |
| `magnitude` | `uint64`          | the absolute value to render   |
| `negative`  | `bool`            | whether the value is negative  |

**Returns**: success when the complete rendering was accepted
